answer: At a desert oasis, each agent tends one yarrow sprig at one well's rim and keeps one numbered onyx pebble in the well bucket. Each morning the agent draws the bucket, reads the pebble against the well log, and waters the sprig from it. At dusk a second keeper checks the sprig is alive and the pebble is still in the bucket, and strikes any name whose plant wilted or whose pebble is gone. A thousand fake names need a thousand watered sprigs and a thousand numbered pebbles, and one pair of hands cannot haul a thousand buckets before the sun dries the rim.
